jobs.occupation: Managing Director (m/f/d) SCHOTTEL France S.A.R.L. (Remote within France), SCHOTTEL France (Art-Director)
jobs.description: Welcome on board at SCHOTTEL France S.A.R.L. SCHOTTEL France S.A.R.L. is the French subsidiary of SCHOTTEL GmbH, one of the world's leading manufacturers of propulsion and manoeuvring solutions for the maritime industry. Since 1971, the company has been serving customers in commercial shipping, naval defence, offshore and inland waterway markets, combining local market expertise with the technological strength of the global SCHOTTEL Group. With a strong focus on customer proximity and lifecycle support, SCHOTTEL France delivers complete propulsion solutions for newbuild and retrofit projects, including engineering, technical consulting and project management. The company furthermore provides comprehensive aftermarket services, ranging from spare parts supply and technical support to upgrades, commissioning, diagnostics and the deployment of highly qualified service technicians. Backed by SCHOTTEL's global network and expertise, SCHOTTEL France is committed to ensuring reliable, efficient and sustainable vessel operations throughout the entire product lifecycle. We offer: A key leadership position with a high level of entrepreneurial responsibility Significant scope for shaping and developing the business An international working environment with short decision-making paths Attractive compensation and benefits package with long-term career perspective within a stable and successful group Your key responsibilities include: Overall management of SCHOTTEL France S.A.R.L., leading a small, high-performing team Full responsibility for achieving the strategic and operational targets, including utilization, cost efficiency and overall profitability Leading and developing a small local team through strong strategic and hands-on leadership Managing and developing customer relationships and customer processes in line with corporate guidelines and in close coordination with the board Ensuring efficient, goal-oriented, and cost-effective operational processes while complying with industry standards and corporate policies Planning and implementing local marketing and sales initiatives, such as customer events Ensure alignment with the company's global strategy and collaborate closely with other international subsidiaries Report directly to the Headquarters in Germany Foster a culture of teamwork, accountability and continuous improvement Your profile: Successfully completed a technical degree in Engineering or a commercial degree in Business Administration or a comparable qualification Several years of professional experience in a senior management role, e.g. Branch Manager, Sales Director or Site Manager In-depth knowledge of the maritime industry, including markets, suppliers and customers Proven experience in people management as well as strong knowledge of controlling instruments and P&L responsibility Strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate and develop employees Excellent communication skills and a confident, professional and approachable manner when dealing with employees, customers and suppliers Fluent in English (required) Native French language skills are required Strong communication and negotiation skill Ability to work effectively in an international and intercultural environment Strategic thinker with hands-on mentality   A BOOST FOR CAREERS | SCHOTTEL.DE Have we sparked your interest? If so, we look forward to meeting you.

Core mission:The Institut Laue-Langevin (ILL), situated in Grenoble, France, is Europe's leading research facility for scientific research using neutrons. Every year we host over 2000 visits by scientists, who come to the Institute to carry out world-class research.Under the responsibility of the Head of the Site Security and Protection Service (SSP), which is part of the ILL's Reactor Division, you will help to ensure the safety and security of persons and property on the site. You will assist in the surveillance of the various secured areas on the ILL site and will work in collaboration with the shift teams in the reactor control room.Your tasks:? Perform CCTV site surveillance and alarm handling.? Perform surveillance on the installations.? Initiate and guide specialist emergency or intervention teams.? Issue site access and carry out entry and exit controls at different locations.? Conduct security patrols.? Act as a first responder in the event of a fire and liaise with external emergency services.? Take action upon request by the emergency services or provide assistance to victims.? Perform various alarm verifications.? Process and relay site-security-related information and fill in the service logbook.? Take part in the periodic tests and inspections for which the Site Security and Protection Service is responsible.? Facilitate access as appropriate to the different zones for visitors, researchers and scientists within the responsibility of the SSP.Your profile:? You have a Level 3/4 qualification ('A' level equivalent) in the field of security.? You hold a valid private security guard licence (CNAPS licence, SIA licence or equivalent).? You have solid professional experience in the emergency services (for example, the military, police or fire service), or in the private or public security sector.? You are dynamic and meticulous, follow rules and respect your manager. You thrive on teamwork and demonstrate a high degree of adaptability.? You have no difficulty using computer technology or monitoring technology (screens) required for the job.? You are able to handle stress and remain in control of yourself at all times.? You are able to apply the appropriate procedures and instructions, but can also show initiative and discerning judgment.? An intermediate level of English is desirable. Sound knowledge of French is required.What we offerQuality of life - This position is based in Grenoble, a hub for research and technology, ideally located in the heart of the French Alps (just 3 hours from Paris/Provence by train, 1 hour from Lyon international airport and 1 ½ hours from Geneva). It is important for us that our staff achieve a healthy work-life balance. We therefore offer home working (under certain conditions), generous annual paid leave entitlement and a host of other benefits that you will discover when you arrive!Prospects - We guarantee you a secure permanent position based in Grenoble in a multicultural scientific environment.Benefits - We offer generous social benefits (expatriation allowance, excellent health cover), moving and relocation assistance (under certain conditions) and an annual productivity bonus. We also offer language courses for you and your partner and subsidies for the use of public transport and the staff canteen, as well as for holidays and a variety of cultural and sports activities. For more details, visit https://www.ill.eu/careers/working-at-the-ill/employment-conditions.Sounds interesting?Then why not take your next career step with us by applying online via our career portal by 01/11/2026, quoting reference number 26/45. Please note that all applicants are subject to administrative screening (background checks). For this post, medical fitness (including for work under ionising radiation) is required. You will also have to perform an emergency response role in the event of a crisis. We are committed to equal opportunities and diversity and therefore welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates.

jobs.occupation: Nuclear Quality Assurance Engineer, INB - French basic nuclear installation
jobs.description: Core mission:The Institut Laue-Langevin (ILL), situated in Grenoble, France, is Europe's leading research facility for scientific research using neutrons. Every year we host over 2000 visits by scientists, who come to the Institute to carry out world-class research.The ILL's Quality, Risk Management and Nuclear Safety Unit (CQSR - Cellule Qualité Sûreté Risques) is a small, dynamic team of five people which reports directly to ILL Management. The core mission of the CQSR is to maintain and improve the ILL's Integrated Management System (IMS), which enables the Institute to comply with regulatory requirements for basic nuclear installations (INB - Installation nucléaire de base). This includes aspects relating to nuclear safety and quality management.Your tasks:As quality assurance engineer, you will play an active part in the development and maintenance of the IMS. Your main duties will be to:- Manage the process for monitoring fulfilment of commitments (improvement actions)- Manage the process for monitoring regulatory changes and compliance- Propose solutions to help process managers maintain and improve their processes- Support engineers and technicians with the documentation requirements associated with technical projects to upgrade the facility- Participate in IMS process reviews- Help to lead training sessions on the IMS- Prepare and conduct internal and external quality audits (including field work) on IMS processesOnce you have received training:- Take on the role of contact person for corruption prevention and fraud control officer (information gathering, awareness-raising, whistleblowing contact person)- Perform event analyses from an HOF perspective- Assist with the preparation of the periodic information campaign on industrial hazardsYour profile:- Master's degree (or equivalent) in quality assurance or Master's degree in general engineering with proven experience in quality assurance.- Solid professional experience is required.- Experience in the nuclear sector is required.- Proficiency in the use of MS Office applications (PowerPoint, Excel, etc.).- Excellent writing skills in French.- Well-organised and methodical with a responsive attitude; good teamwork skills.What we offer: Quality of life - This position is based in Grenoble, a hub for research and technology, ideally located in the heart of the French Alps (just 3 hours from Paris/Provence by train, 1 hour from Lyon international airport and 1 ½ hours from Geneva). It is important for us that our staff achieve a healthy work-life balance. We therefore offer home working (under certain conditions), generous annual paid leave entitlement and a host of other benefits that you will discover when you arrive!!Prospects - We guarantee you a secure permanent position based in Grenoble in a multicultural scientific environment.Benefits - We offer generous social benefits (expatriation allowance, excellent health cover), moving and relocation assistance (under certain conditions) and an annual productivity bonus. Please note that all applicants are subject to administrative screening (background checks) and that medical fitness (including for work under ionising radiation) is required for this position. You will also have to perform an emergency response role in the event of a crisis. We are committed to equal opportunities and diversity and therefore welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates.The Institut Laue-Langevin (ILL), situated in Grenoble, France, is Europe's leading research facility for fundamental research using neutrons. United by our passion for progress and technology, we drive science and research forward every day. Together, we can pave the way for discoveries that will help to make our world a better place.
